subject: sarf
definition: A verb or noun with one or more letters added to its root letters, which usually change or add to its meaning.
explanation: From عَلِمَ (he knew) come عَلَّمَ (he taught), with a doubled ʿayn, and تَعَلَّمَ (he learnt), with a tāʾ in front as well. Each added pattern has meanings it often carries: أَفْعَلَ often makes a verb transitive, and تَفَاعَلَ often shows an act done to one another.
Grammars written in Europe number these patterns II to X. The madrasa books name them by their maṣdar: bāb al-tafʿīl for فَعَّلَ, bāb al-ifʿāl for أَفْعَلَ, bāb al-istifʿāl for اِسْتَفْعَلَ.

examples.english: karuma, he was noble; akrama, he honoured: a hamza is added.
ʿalima, he knew; taʿallama, he learnt: a tāʾ and a doubled ʿayn are added.
